strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-21426: scipy.special.betaincinv returns NaN for float32 inputs a=b=5, x=0.5 on a SciPy built with the older Boost submodule (54e5acf7). The developer's test test_gh21426 (float32 and float64) should fail on the buggy build and pass once the PR-fixed build with Boost 260f7600 is compiled. Environment era is numpy 2.1.x and scipy 1.14.x; the Boost pin is unbounded in the evidence, so the strategy pins it to the two submodule commits named in the PR diff.

build_commands: git checkout <PR-21678 head commit that updates boost_math>
pinned_because: numpy 2.1.0 is an era inference from issue#21426 system information, not a documented requirement; kept to match the reporter
scipy 1.14.x is an era inference; the reproduction is run from the source tree at the buggy commit, so the scipy version is determined by the checkout rather than pip

boost_math is unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era entry); this plan pins it to the buggy submodule commit 54e5acf7 and the fixed commit 260f7600 taken from the PR diff, which is the choice being relied on

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_basic.py::TestBetainc::test_gh21426 (parametrized over float32 and float64); the class name is inferred from placement after test_betainc_domain_errors
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (boost_math at 54e5acf7) the float32 case of test_gh21426 FAILS because betaincinv returns NaN and assert_allclose reports a mismatch against 0.5; on the fixed revision (boost_math at 260f7600) both float32 and float64 cases PASS. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Before running the test, confirm the built extension imports and that scipy.special.betaincinv accepts float32 arrays; this is a build-state check only and is not the pass/fail transition.

input_output_examples.input: a = np.array([[5]], dtype='f'); x = np.array([[0.5]], dtype='f'); scipy.special.betaincinv(a, a, x)
a = np.array([5.], dtype=np.float32); x = np.array([0.5], dtype=np.float32); special.betaincinv(a, a, x)

risks: The NaN is reported as occurring only occasionally, so it may depend on the platform, compiler, or float32 code path; on a platform where it does not occur the buggy build may not fail and the test would not transition.

The reproduction is only known on the x86_64 Linux-style build implied by the report; a 32-bit architecture would need the looser tolerance that is not stated in the evidence, so the test given here (rtol=10*eps) is the only one planned.
The fixed-commit hash is not given in the evidence; it must be taken from the PR head that updates scipy/_lib/boost_math to 260f7600e95d.
The loosened 32-bit/single-precision tolerance is not stated, so it cannot be used as a fallback oracle.
Behaviour depends on the Boost version; if the submodule is not checked out to 54e5acf7 on the buggy revision, NaN may not reproduce and the test could pass for the wrong reason.
No BLAS/LAPACK is documented for this path, so the reproduction assumes the Boost-backed special function alone determines the result.
Build time for SciPy from source is long; the two builds are required for the transition and cannot be replaced by a pip-installed wheel.

oracle.reference_source: test_gh21426 in the PR diff, asserting result close to x=0.5
oracle.why: With a=b the regularized incomplete beta is symmetric so the inverse at x=0.5 is exactly 0.5; the tolerance is dtype-specific per the PR

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy Boost (54e5acf7) the float32 call returns NaN; assert_allclose compares NaN to 0.5 with default equal_nan semantics (only NaN-vs-NaN matches), so the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed Boost (260f7600) betaincinv returns a value within 10*eps of 0.5 for float32 and float64, so assert_allclose passes.
